topics.label: Imitation learning foundations for robot control
topics.summary: The core ideas of behavior cloning, covariate shift, and end-to-end visuomotor learning that every modern manipulation policy rests on.

claims.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
claims.rationale: Introduces DAgger and formalizes compounding error under covariate shift; the reference point for why naive behavior cloning fails and what later data-collection schemes are trying to fix.

claims.title: End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies
claims.rationale: First convincing demonstration that a single network can map raw pixels to motor torques for manipulation; establishes the pixels-to-actions framing that VLAs scale up.

claims.title: An Algorithmic Perspective on Imitation Learning
claims.rationale: Comprehensive survey of behavior cloning and inverse RL for robotics; a map of the pre-deep-learning landscape and the vocabulary used in later papers.

topics.label: Visuomotor policy learning from demonstrations
topics.summary: Modern single-task policies trained on human teleoperation data, with the architectural choices (action chunking, diffusion heads) that carried into generalist models.

claims.title: What Matters in Learning from Offline Human Demonstrations for Robot Manipulation
claims.rationale: The robomimic study: a careful empirical dissection of which design choices matter for behavior cloning on real teleop data, and the benchmark later papers compare against.

claims.title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
claims.rationale: Introduces ACT (action chunking with transformers) and the ALOHA teleop rig; action chunking is now standard in nearly every VLA.

claims.title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
claims.rationale: Models the action distribution with a diffusion process to handle multimodal demonstrations; the direct ancestor of the diffusion and flow-matching action heads in Octo and π0.

topics.label: Language-conditioned policies and large-scale robot data
topics.summary: Scaling imitation learning across many tasks and robots with language instructions and large multi-task datasets, setting up the data regime VLAs need.

claims.title: BC-Z: Zero-Shot Task Generalization with Robotic Imitation Learning
claims.rationale: Early evidence that conditioning a visuomotor policy on language or video embeddings yields zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks given enough demonstrations.

claims.title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
claims.rationale: A transformer trained on 130k real-robot episodes across 700+ tasks; shows tokenized actions and scale drive generalization, and is the base RT-2 builds on.

claims.title: BridgeData V2: A Dataset for Robot Learning at Scale
claims.rationale: The most widely used open real-robot dataset; understanding its structure and evaluation protocol is needed to read OpenVLA, Octo, and SIMPLER results.

claims.title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
claims.rationale: Pools 22 robot embodiments into one dataset and shows cross-embodiment co-training improves RT-1/RT-2; the data substrate for OpenVLA, Octo, and π0.

topics.label: Vision-language-action models
topics.summary: Fine-tuning pretrained vision-language models to emit robot actions, transferring web-scale semantic knowledge into manipulation policies.

claims.title: PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model
claims.rationale: Injects robot sensor data into a large language model for embodied planning; the VLM backbone RT-2 adapts and the conceptual bridge from LLMs to action.

claims.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control
claims.rationale: Coins the term VLA: represents actions as text tokens and co-fine-tunes a VLM on web and robot data, yielding emergent semantic generalization. The paper that defines the field.

claims.title: Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy
claims.rationale: Open generalist policy trained on Open X-Embodiment with a diffusion action head and modular tokenizers; a counterpoint to VLM-backbone VLAs and easy to fine-tune.

claims.title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
claims.rationale: The open reproduction of the RT-2 recipe on a 7B Prismatic VLM; its ablations on backbones, fine-tuning, and quantization make it the practical reference for building a VLA.

claims.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
claims.rationale: Replaces discrete action tokens with a flow-matching action expert on a PaliGemma backbone, enabling 50 Hz dexterous bimanual control; merges the diffusion-policy and VLA lines.

claims.title: A Survey on Vision-Language-Action Models for Embodied AI
claims.rationale: Taxonomy of VLA components (pretraining, control policies, task planners) with a catalogue of models and datasets; useful for placing the core papers in context.

topics.label: Evaluation, benchmarks, and open-world generalization
topics.summary: How generalist policies are measured and where the frontier is pushing: reproducible evaluation and transfer to unseen environments and embodiments.

claims.title: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning
claims.rationale: The simulation benchmark most VLA papers report on (LIBERO-Spatial/Object/Goal/Long); needed to interpret the numbers in OpenVLA, π0, and successors.

claims.title: Evaluating Real-World Robot Manipulation Policies in Simulation
claims.rationale: SIMPLER: simulated evaluation that correlates with real-robot success for RT-1, RT-2, and Octo; addresses the reproducibility problem that makes VLA comparisons hard.

claims.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
claims.rationale: Co-trains on heterogeneous web, multi-robot, and subtask-prediction data to clean unseen homes; the current reference for what open-world generalization in VLAs looks like.

claims.title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
claims.rationale: Dual-system VLA (VLM reasoner plus diffusion action module) trained on a mix of real, simulated, and human-video data; shows the design space beyond single-backbone VLAs.
